title: Two-headed planarian state persists through further cutting despite wild-type genome

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Two-headed planarian state persists through further cutting despite wild-type genome

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Planaria with abnormal head number induced by transient bioelectric manipulation are permanently altered: when cut into pieces with no further treatment, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number despite wild-type genetics.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Remarkably, the worms with abnormal head number are permanently altered to this pattern, despite their wild-type genetics: cut into pieces with no further manipulations, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number (Oviedo et al., 2010; Durant et al., 2017).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops”. Scope: Planarians after transient gap-junction blockade (e.g. octanol) and serial amputation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The serial-regeneration criterion is clear and distinguishes transient morphology from inherited state. Published experiments cover the central result, but data access and the unbounded word 'permanently' limit full resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track head number across serial amputations after transient treatment has ended, compare with vehicle controls, and verify unchanged genotype; persistence across untreated rounds supports a stable non-genetic state.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Residual treatment or stable tissue changes must be excluded.

Complete worm-level lineage records may not be public.

Permanence is bounded by the observed regeneration rounds.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.86
data adequacy: 0.48

operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head counts across amputation rounds with no further treatment are published for the octanol and related protocols. Planform may contain the curated head-number outcomes; it does not replace the raw counts. Persistence can be checked at the level of those published penetrances, and the genetic-wild-type clause stays weakly tested without sequence of the same lines.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Cut transiently treated two-headed or zero-headed worms with no further drug and score head number in successive regenerates, alongside a wild-type sequence or drug-residue assay; persistence holds if abnormal head number continues after the drug is gone and the genome matches wild type.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Residual drug or a selected genetic variant can mimic a permanent physiological state.

Wild-type genome is argued from induction and reset experiments more often than from deposited sequence of the altered lines.

Penetrance tables are in the papers, not as animal-level files.
